newsitem.title: DUBAI: Third oil tanker arrives at Mina al-Bakr -source.
newsitem.headline: Third oil tanker arrives at Mina al-Bakr -source.

text.p: An oil tanker berthed at Iraq's Mina al-Bakr export terminal on Sunday, the third vessel at the Gulf terminal under the United Nations "oil-for-food" deal with Baghdad, a Gulf-based shipping source said on Sunday.
The first two cargoes of Iraqi oil from Mina al-Bakr were exported by American firms Coastal Corp and Bayoil on December 17 and December 19.
The name of the newly arrived tanker and its charterer were not immediately known.
Japanese, Russian and U.S. firms have U.N. approved contracts to lift Iraqi Basrah Light crude from al-Bakr.
Japan's Mitsubishi fixed a tanker to load under a 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) contract for five Japanese firms.
The U.N. has approved 21 crude contracts for a total of just over 500,000 bpd.
Under the U.N. deal, Iraq is allowed to export $2 billion of its oil over six months on a renewal basis in exchange for food and other humanitarian supplies.
The Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan accounts for the bulk of Iraq's exports, the first since Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation has scheduled nine cargoes totalling about eight million barrels, or 260,000 bpd, to be exported from Ceyhan in January.
